chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yahya ibn al-Hajjaj, from Khalid ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who had a debt of one hundred dirhams by number upon him, so he paid me one hundred dirhams by weight. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, provided there was no stipulation.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Usury arises from the stipulations; it is the stipulations that spoil it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a debt of 100 dirhams by number with 100 dirhams by weight?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that repaying a counted debt with weighed currency is permissible provided no prior condition (shart) created an imbalance, illustrating the Shia juristic principle that riba in such exchanges is contingent upon stipulated terms rather than the mere change in measurement. It highlights the distinction between natural market fluctuations and contractual usury, a key concept in fiqh al-mu'amalat. The Imam’s statement that 'riba comes from the conditions' underscores the importance of contractual intent in determining the validity of the transaction.
